identity.title: ALMA Observation of the Protoplanetary Disk around WW Cha: Faint Double-peaked Ring and Asymmetric Structure

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we report dust continuum observations of the disk around WW Cha in ALMA Cycle 5.

evidence.quote: Our target, WW Cha is a young star with a circumstellar disk (cite: Pascucci2016; Garufi2020) in the Chameleon I star-forming region.
The star is located at about 190 pc (cite: GaiaDR2; GaiaEDR3).
Our target, WW Cha is a young star with a circumstellar disk (cite: Pascucci2016; Garufi2020) in the Chameleon I star-forming region.
The star is located at about 190 pc (cite: GaiaDR2; GaiaEDR3).

question.value: Resolve disk substructures and constrain dust density, temperature, and grain-size distribution around WW Cha.

evidence.quote: To examine the structure of the disk in detail, we performed fitting for dust continuum emission in the visibility domain with a simple disk model.

In this section, we discuss the physical condition (e.g., dust surface density, size distribution of the dust grains, and temperature) of the disk, by using radiative transfer simulations with RADMC-3D
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00286.S.
The observation was carried out by ALMA in band 6

claims.hypothesis: Does WW Cha contain a large cavity, gaps, or radial dust substructure?

claims.experiment: Compare axisymmetric-model residuals with imaginary-visibility images.
claims.result: Both methods recover central and outer asymmetric structures.
claims.finding: The asymmetries are supported independently of the radial intensity model.

evidence.quote: The residual map between the model and observation indicates asymmetric structures at the center and the outer region of the disk.

claims.experiment: Use radiative-transfer temperatures at the fitted peak locations.
claims.result: Outer and inner peak temperatures are about 30 K and 50 K.

evidence.quote: the temperature around the outer peak is about $30$ K, which is close to the freezeout temperature of CO at water ice (cite: Huang_DSHARP).
Around the inner peak, the temperature is about $50$ K.
Hence, this bump with double peaks may be formed by the snowline and the sintering effect.

The faint positive structure at the upper left might be explained by the gravitational instability if the disk is marginally stable with a smaller gas-to-dust ratio.

Because of this difference between the C43-4 and C43-8 data, the reduced $\chi^2$ of the best fit model is much deviated from unity, when the data are combined.
If only C43-4 data is used, the resolution is not enough to identify substructures.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: A pressure bump or planetary-gap dust trap is disfavored by the double peak and absence of an interior gap.

evidence.quote: However, the bump that is formed by the above mechanisms likely has a single peak, while the bump of our model has double peaks.
However, we did not detect any gap structure interior to the bump structure.
Hence, it might not be the structure induced by the dust trap of the pressure bump and planetary gap.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: L* = 11 L⊙ needs an envelope contribution to infrared flux; L* = 22 L⊙ reproduces infrared-to-radio fluxes without that contribution.

evidence.quote: In the case with $L_{\ast}=11L_{\odot}$, the flux at far infrared wavelengths is about a factor of two smaller than the observed values.
In this case, we need some contribution from the envelope to account for infrared flux.
the case with $L_{\ast}=22L_{\odot}$ can reproduce the fluxes from the infrared to the radio, by only the emission from the star.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Power-law large-grain distributions do not reproduce the within-band central index below 2; a log-normal distribution may be preferred there.

evidence.quote: With the power-law distribution, the spectral index does not become below 2, even if the maximum size of the dust grains is 0.5 mm.
Hence, the log-normal size distribution of large grains may be preferred for the inner region.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Vortex dust trapping may struggle to produce such a faint asymmetry.

evidence.quote: Such a faint structure might be difficult to be formed by the dust trap into the vortex.

evidence.quote: Alternatively, we cannot see significant spiral pattern because the disk is optically thick.

Since the star has a high accretion rate, the asymmetry may be associated to the accretion variability or a jet.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Restrict fitting to visibilities above the effective noise limit; iterate radiative transfer to temperature convergence.

evidence.quote: Since the amplitude of the visibility is comparable with the noise level in $\rho>2000k\lambda$, we used the visibility in the range of $\rho < 2000k\lambda$ in this modeling.

referee_caveats_inferred: The observations and fitting sections reverse the 10/20 kλ bin assignments around 1200 kλ.
The paper names vis_simple once and vis_sample elsewhere; the exact model-sampling call needs clarification.
Formal MCMC errors do not establish robustness to flux calibration, binning, or the adopted radial-profile family.
Grain-size and instability interpretations depend on opacity, luminosity, vertical structure, and gas-to-dust assumptions.
The stated dust masses do not scale exactly with the stated factor-of-two change in Σ0.
The central asymmetry is sensitive to milliarcsecond recentering, and the cavity is unresolved.
Table 1 gives 4.0 GHz continuum bandwidth, whereas the text describes two 1.875 GHz SPWs.
